preamble: Loss of the rhotic approximant [ɹ] outside prevocalic position, known as non-rhoticity. Loss of postvocalic r began in England in the 15th century, and by the early 19th century the southern English standard was fully non-rhotic. Non-rhotic accents now include most of England, Wales, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa, as well as African American Vernacular English. Before a vowel the r is kept as linking [ɹ] (water ice).

examples.from: Early Modern English car, with coda r (still [ɹ] in rhotic accents)
examples.note: Non-rhotic accents lost the coda rhotic, leaving a long or lengthened vowel; before a vowel the r is still pronounced as linking r.

examples.from: Early Modern English hard, with coda r
